fx_path.source: Egyptian pound per US dollar, FY2026E-FY2030E period averages. Built from the inflation differential rather than asserted: the pound averaged 47.74 in 2024 and 49.48 in 2025 (a 3.6% move) while consumer inflation ran far above the United States', so the real exchange rate appreciated. The path assumes that reverses only partially, at roughly 4% a year narrowing to 3% as domestic inflation converges on the central bank's stated 5% medium-term target

dom_pack_growth.source: Domestic packs sold, annual volume growth FY2026E-FY2030E. The company sold 244.3 million domestic packs of its own preparations in FY2024 and 291.8 million in FY2025 (+19.5%); disclosed capacity utilisation is 65% of 3,383 million units, so the volume is not capacity-constrained. The path steps down from a rate materially below the FY2025 outturn toward population-plus-penetration growth. THE FIRST YEAR IS RESET TO THE FIRST QUARTER'S OUTTURN: net sales grew 10.1% year on year in the three months to March 2026, against the 17.5% the first cut of this model carried

exp_pack_growth.source: Export packs, annual volume growth. Export value grew 10% in US dollars in FY2025 (USD 54.7m to 60.0m) on a company that is already the largest Egyptian pharmaceutical exporter with 26% of national pharmaceutical export value across 67 countries; the biosimilars plant licensed in December 2025 adds a new export line rather than replacing one

dom_price_growth.source: Domestic realised price per pack, annual growth. Egyptian medicine prices are set administratively by the Egyptian Drug Authority and move in periodic approved adjustments rather than continuously; realised price per pack rose 12.6% in FY2025 after a much larger devaluation-driven step in FY2024. The path assumes price growth tracks domestic inflation as it converges on the central bank's target, with no real price gain

exp_price_usd_growth.source: Export realised price per pack in US dollars, annual growth. FY2025 realised USD 1.00 per pack. Generic export pricing is competitive and broadly flat in hard currency; 1% a year is a nominal-dollar drift, not a real gain

toll_growth.source: Contract-manufacturing revenue growth. A small line (0.5% of revenue) that grew 37.8% in FY2025 off a low base as the company let third parties use idle capacity

cost_shares.source: Audited consolidated financial statements for the year ended 31 December 2025, published in the company's 2025 Annual Report (eipico.com.eg -> Investor Relations -> Annual Reports), cost of sales note (26). esc_materials_usd.source: Active pharmaceutical ingredient input prices in US dollars, annual escalation. esc_packaging_import_share.source: Share of the packaging cost line that is imported input (aluminium foil, film, closures) and therefore escalates on the hard-currency path; the balance is produced in-house by the group's own ampoule and plastics factories and escalates domestically

esc_labour.source: Egyptian wage escalation. Headcount grew 2% in FY2025 while the wage bill in cost of sales grew 27%, so unit labour cost is rising faster than consumer prices as the statutory minimum wage is reset; the path decays toward domestic inflation

esc_energy.source: Egyptian regulated energy and utility tariffs, escalated ABOVE consumer inflation for the near term because the subsidy-reform programme resets industrial electricity and gas tariffs on its own schedule; a domestic consumer-price proxy would understate it

esc_domestic_cpi.source: Egyptian consumer price inflation path, applied only to genuinely domestic service and consumable lines. Converges on the central bank's stated 5-7% medium-term target band

mkt_pct.source: Selling and marketing expense as a share of revenue. The disclosed ratio fell from 12.9% (FY2023) to 12.4% (FY2024) to 10.7% (FY2025) as the company got operating leverage on a larger sales base; the path assumes that gain is largely banked but not extended much further

rnd_pct.source: Research and development as a share of revenue, rising modestly from the FY2025 level of 0.75% as the biosimilars pipeline moves through registration

ga_pct.source: General and administrative expense as a share of revenue, held near the FY2025 level of 2.34%

prov_pct_permanent.source: Credit losses, inventory write-downs and other provisions as a permanent share of revenue — the FRAME A reading. LABEL CORRECTED: this is NOT 'the three-year average', which the earlier edition called it. The disclosed charge runs 5.07% (FY2023), 9.24% (FY2024), 5.23% (FY2025); the mean of those three ratios is 6.52% and the mean of the two years either side of the FY2024 spike is 5.15%. 5.25% IS STRUCK MARGINALLY ABOVE THE TWO NON-OUTLIER YEARS, and that is what it should be called. Both the 6.52% three-year mean and the 3.03% expected-credit-loss-only three-year mean are published beside it and the frame is sensitised across them. Context that neither reading carries: the first quarter of 2026 booked NO expected credit loss at all — one of the three matters the auditor qualified — so 6.52% is more than twice a quarter that charged nothing

prov_pct_normalising.source: The FRAME B reading of the same charge: a receivable and inventory book that is seasoning, with the charge decaying toward the 2.5% of revenue that a distributor-concentrated generic book carries in steady state. Both frames are carried through the whole model and published side by side; neither is averaged into the other

capex_pct.source: Capital expenditure as a share of revenue. cip_transfer.source: Transfers out of projects under construction into depreciable property, EGP million. This is the single largest mechanical change in the forecast income statement

dep_rate.source: Average annual depreciation rate on the depreciable property base. dio.source: Inventory days on cost of sales. The audited FY2025 position implies 268 days. dso.source: Trade receivable days on revenue. The audited FY2025 position implies 129 days, against 147 days in FY2024, reflecting a distributor-concentrated domestic book and export terms; the path continues the improvement already underway

dpo.source: Trade payable days on cost of sales. The audited FY2025 position implies 54 days, up from 36 days in FY2024

A live re-read of the central bank's own fixed-coupon treasury bond auction page was attempted on 09-Aug-2026 and rejected by that site's web application firewall, so the level is indicated by a market-data series rather than proven from the auction curve — and it is sensitised

sov_spread_rating.source: Egypt adjusted default spread on the rating basis (Moody's Caa1), 5.9702%, same mid-year (July 2026) vintage, 'Rating-based Default Spread' column — the alternative construction, published for the audit trail. The January-2026 vintage carried 6.3725%

erp_cds.source: Egypt TOTAL equity risk premium on the sovereign-CDS basis, 9.5164%, same mid-year vintage. This is the dataset's TOTAL equity risk premium column, not its country risk premium column — the total premium is what multiplies beta. The CDS-basis country risk premium alone is 5.3164%

erp_rating.source: Egypt TOTAL equity risk premium on the rating basis, 13.4806%, same mid-year vintage — again the TOTAL equity risk premium column, being the 9.2806% country risk premium over a 4.20% mature-market premium. The January-2026 vintage carried 13.9377% total over a 9.7077% country premium

crp_rating.source: Egypt COUNTRY risk premium on the rating basis, 9.2806%, mid-year (July 2026) vintage — carried separately and published beside the total premium so that a reader checking the dataset's own 'Country Risk Premium' column finds the figure this study calls by that name. It is NOT added to the cost of equity; the total premium above already contains it

crp_cds.source: Egypt COUNTRY risk premium on the sovereign-CDS basis, 5.3164%, mid-year vintage, disclosure only — see the note above

beta.source: Own-stock first-tier regression: weekly logarithmic returns of the company's own shares against an equal-weighted composite of 36 Egyptian listed names built from the full covered price library, five-year window. R-squared 0.235, n = 257, standard error 0.071, 90% confidence interval [0.51, 0.75]. Clears every usability test on every limb and is not weak-instrument flagged. A beta well below one is what a defensive, price-regulated, domestically-consumed staple should produce

kd_egp.source: Marginal cost of local-currency debt: the ten-year sovereign yield of 22.31% plus a 250 basis-point corporate credit spread. A same-currency corporate cannot borrow below its own sovereign, so this is floored at the sovereign yield by construction

kd_fx_coupon.source: Marginal coupon on the group's hard-currency borrowings. Half the term-loan book is US-dollar and euro paper from Qatar National Bank Alahli and the National Bank of Kuwait; 7.5% is the dollar-funding cost for an unrated Egyptian corporate at current benchmark rates

fx_dep_wacc.source: Expected annual depreciation of the Egyptian pound used to carry foreign-currency debt at its LOCAL-EQUIVALENT cost. Taken from the model's own exchange-rate path (50.5 to 57.7 over five years, a 3.4% compound rate) with a margin; a raw hard-currency coupon inside a pound-nominal weighted average cost of capital would understate the cost of that debt

int_path.source: Finance cost charged to the income statement, EGP million. This is NOT the marginal cost of debt used in the discount rate — that is a forward, local-equivalent, currency-blended rate; this is what the profit and loss account actually bears, and part of the group's interest is still being capitalised into the remaining construction balance. CALIBRATED TO THE FIRST QUARTER OF 2026: 312.862 of financing expense in three months, DOWN 6.9% year on year, an annual run-rate of about 1,251 against the 1,548 the first cut of this model implied. It then declines with the central bank's easing cycle

kd_path.source: CONVERGENCE PATH, FY2026E-FY2030E. This row is NOT the cost of local-currency debt (24.81%) and NOT the blended marginal cost of debt (18.55%): its first point, 18.90%, is the NORMALISED RISK-FREE RATE, and the row traces that rate converging on the terminal norm as the central bank's easing cycle runs. Its only job is to give the discount-rate glide a shape derived from something in the model rather than an invented curve; the glide uses the row normalised to its own endpoints, so the levels cancel and only the SHAPE enters. The earlier edition described it as a cost-of-debt path, which it is not

rf_term.source: Terminal risk-free rate, built from norms rather than extrapolated: the central bank's stated medium-term inflation target of 5% plus the standard 5.5-point emerging-market real-rate convention

erp_term.source: Terminal equity risk premium, normalised below today's crisis-era level toward the rating-class norm; never held flat into perpetuity

kd_term_lc.source: Terminal local-currency corporate borrowing rate — the long-run Egyptian norm of roughly 10 points above the 5% inflation target

wd_term_basis.source: Basis on which the TERMINAL debt weight is set. It is no longer an asserted 20%. The earlier edition claimed 20% was 'reconciled to the model's own forecast balance sheet'; it was not — that sheet, once it is made to balance, carries a book net-debt weight near 39% at FY2030E, and today's market-value net-debt weight is near 25%. Neither is 20%, and the stated deleveraging never happens once the forecast is funded. This input selects which reconcilable reading is used: 'market' takes today's market-value net-debt weight (the weighting basis a weighted average cost of capital requires), 'book' takes the forecast terminal book weight. Both are computed below and both are published

g_term.source: Terminal growth, 5% — an Egyptian-pound NOMINAL rate struck against a terminal risk-free rate that itself embeds 5% inflation, so the base case assumes approximately zero real terminal growth. Deliberately conservative for a company with a third of its revenue in hard currency and a biosimilars plant just entering service. Sensitised 3-7%

roic_term_source.source: Terminal return on invested capital is no longer an input. The earlier edition asserted 20% while the model's own FY2030E return on invested capital was 16.36% — a 364 basis-point step up, taken at exactly the point where three quarters of core enterprise value sits. The terminal return is now COMPUTED as the model's own final forecast year, so terminal reinvestment (growth divided by return) cannot assume a return the forecast does not earn. narrative: [History] the audited consolidated income statement reconstructs line-by-line for all three years: revenue less cost of sales less operating expenses less the provision charge, plus associates, interest income, exchange differences and other income, less finance costs, equals disclosed pre-tax profit to within EGP 0.02 million in each year.
FY2023: revenue 5,232 · gross margin 44.6% · provision charge 5.07% of revenue · EBIT 1,229 (23.5%) · EBITDA 1,335 · net profit 823 · effective tax 24.0%
FY2024: revenue 7,591 · gross margin 44.9% · provision charge 9.25% of revenue · EBIT 1,529 (20.1%) · EBITDA 1,631 · net profit 1,097 · effective tax 28.3%
FY2025: revenue 9,441 · gross margin 44.0% · provision charge 5.23% of revenue · EBIT 2,366 (25.1%) · EBITDA 2,484 · net profit 1,458 · effective tax 18.8%

[Unit build] The board report splits the same separate-company revenue two ways, and the two only reconcile once contract manufacturing is separated out. FY2025 sales of the company's OWN preparations were EGP 9,160.148 million on 351.810 million packs; preparations made under CONTRACT for third parties were EGP 142.321 million of product value on 5.485 million packs, of which the company books only the manufacturing fee of EGP 49.366 million — EGP 9.00 a pack — while the remaining EGP 92.955 million reaches the market through its own domestic channels at EGP 16.95 a pack. The two splits sum to the same EGP 9,302.469 million.

LINE 1, own preparations sold at home: 291.810 million packs carrying EGP 6,192.668 million, EGP 21.2216 a pack against EGP 18.8479 in FY2024 — realised price +12.59% on volume +19.46%. Dividing the CHANNEL domestic figure of EGP 6,286 million by these packs instead would read EGP 21.5401 a pack, because that figure carries the contract-made product as well; the difference is 1.50% on the price and it flows into every forecast year.
LINE 2, own preparations exported: 60.000 million packs at EGP 49.46 a pack, which is USD 0.9996 at the disclosed average rate of 49.48 — against USD 0.9574 in FY2024.

LINE 3, contract manufacturing: packs fell 38.2% to 5.485 million while the fee per pack rose 122.9% to EGP 9.00. This is a small line — 1.53% of revenue — but it is forecast on its own volume and its own price rather than folded into the domestic book.
Production ran at 2,208 million units against 3,383 million of disclosed capacity — 65% utilisation, so the volume path below is not capacity-constrained.
Reconstructed channel revenue 9,302.469 against the disclosed separate-company revenue total of 9,302.469 — a difference of 0.000, which is rounding on the incentive lines.

[Consolidation] the reconstructed channel build is a separate-company total; the audited consolidated revenue is 1.0149 times it, the subsidiary's external sales. That measured factor, not an assumption, carries the build to a consolidated basis.

[Cost stack] every physically distinct cost line carries its OWN escalator: imported active ingredients (54.9% of production cost) and the imported share of packaging escalate on a hard-currency price path passed through the exchange-rate path; labour on Egyptian wage growth; energy on the regulated tariff schedule, which runs above consumer inflation; domestic services on consumer inflation. No single blended index is applied across them. Depreciation is excluded here and enters exactly once, from the property roll-forward.
Gross margin path (after the production share of depreciation): FY2025 actual 44.0% -> 41.3% -> 40.6% -> 40.8% -> 41.0% -> 41.1%

[Depreciation] the EGP 4,901 million construction balance stops being free. Transfers of 3,400 / 1,100 million in the first two years take the depreciation charge from an audited FY2025 118 million to 304 then 423 million. That step is the single largest mechanical change in the forecast income statement and it is a consequence of the company's own disclosed licensing timetable, not a view.
EBITDA (cash costs only) FY2026E 2,573 -> FY2030E 4,317 on Frame A; EBIT 2,269 -> 3,894 after the depreciation step.

[Asset-conversion cycle] the audited FY2025 balance sheet implies 268 inventory days, 129 receivable days and 54 payable days — a cash cycle of 343 days. The inventory position is policy: the company stated at its March-2026 general assembly that it holds a strategic raw-material stockpile sufficient for at least eight months. Working capital is PROJECTED from those three ratios, not plugged.

[Funding] the forecast balance sheet is FUNDED, not frozen. Cash is held at the audited 1,433 million operating minimum and gross borrowings carry the difference, so total assets equal total liabilities and equity in every forecast year by construction. Borrowings run 10,079 -> 10,230 -> 9,987 -> 9,561 -> 8,894 against an audited 8,798: the working-capital build and the first year's capital expenditure are debt-funded while a 40% payout continues, and the book only returns to its opening level in the final year. The earlier edition held both cash and borrowings flat, which left the statement out by up to 7.1% of total assets.

CONSEQUENCE, STATED RATHER THAN HIDDEN: on this funded book the finance cost charged in the income statement implies an average borrowing rate of 13.24% / 11.92% / 11.38% / 11.15% / 11.16%, against a blended MARGINAL cost of debt of 18.55% used in the discount rate. The charged path is calibrated to the first quarter of 2026 and is right for FY2026E; the later years assume an easing cycle the debt schedule does not evidence. That gap is an open item, it is not resolved in this edition, and the EARNINGS-BASED lenses are sensitised across it.

[Cost of equity] the quoted ten-year local-currency government yield is 23.00%. That yield is not riskless: it embeds the sovereign's own default risk. Subtracting the sovereign credit-default-swap spread of 3.42% leaves a normalised risk-free rate of 19.58%; adding beta 0.629 times the country equity risk premium of 9.52% gives a cost of equity of 25.57%. On the rating basis the same construction gives 25.51% — the two agree to 6 basis points, which is reassuring because they are built from different columns of the same source. Charging the raw 23.00% yield AND a country-loaded premium would give 28.99% and would count sovereign risk twice; that construction is not used.

[Cost of debt] the term-loan note splits the book 50% local currency / 50% hard currency. The local-currency leg is priced at 24.81% — the sovereign yield plus 250 basis points, and above the sovereign by construction. The hard-currency leg carries a 7.50% coupon but is charged at its LOCAL-EQUIVALENT cost of 12.34%, coupon compounded with expected currency depreciation of 4.50%. Blended marginal cost of debt 18.55%, 14.38% after tax.

[Cost-of-debt integrity] the company expensed 1,275 million of interest and capitalised a further 551 million into the construction balance in FY2025. On average gross debt of 8,999 million that is 14.2% expensed and 20.3% all-in. The 18.5% marginal rate sits inside that pair, which is the test: a marginal rate below the expensed rate or above the all-in rate would not be credible.

Two FY2025 figures are in play here and they are not the same line: INTEREST ON CREDIT FACILITIES of 1,275.312 million, which is what an interest RATE must be computed on, and the income statement's FINANCE COSTS of 1,332.947 million, which is that interest plus 57.634 million of bank commissions and charges. Both come from the same note; the bridge between them is stated here so that neither reads as a contradiction of the other.

[Weighted average cost of capital] market capitalisation 21,947 against net debt 7,364 gives weights 74.9% equity / 25.1% debt and a starting discount rate of 22.75%. On GROSS debt the weights are 71.4%/28.6% and the rate 22.36%; both are published. Note the starting rate sits close to the quoted sovereign yield — that is arithmetic, not an error: the quoted yield contains default risk that the normalised build strips out and re-charges inside the equity premium.

[Terminal] cost of equity 14.90% (risk-free 10.50% plus beta times a normalised 7.00% premium); cost of debt 12.34%, 9.56% after tax; DERIVED debt weight 25.1% on today's market values (39.8% on the funded forecast balance sheet at FY2030E) -> terminal discount rate 13.56% (12.77% on the book weight).

[Discount-rate glide] the fractions are the cost-of-debt path normalised to its own endpoints — 1.000, 0.732, 0.439, 0.195, 0.000 — so the glide has the shape of the easing cycle rather than a shape invented for it. Discount rates 22.75%, 20.29%, 17.60%, 15.35%, 13.56%; the factors compound.

[Terminal consistency] terminal reinvestment is growth 5% divided by the model's OWN FY2030E return on invested capital — 16.03% on Frame A and 18.00% on Frame B — so 31.2% of terminal operating profit after tax is reinvested on Frame A. There is no terminal return assumption left to make. The earlier edition asserted 20% here, a 397 basis-point step above the last forecast year, taken at exactly the point where three quarters of core enterprise value sits.

The terminal year is also charged the depreciation the forecast never charged: 2,955 million of construction is still parked at FY2030E and has never entered the depreciable base, so at the model's own 6.2% rate a further 183 million a year is deducted before the perpetuity is struck. A steady state cannot capitalise profit on capital it never charges.

[Terminal weight] the terminal value is 74% of CORE enterprise value on Frame A and 75% on Frame B — 62% and 64% of TOTAL enterprise value, which carries the associates and the assets held for sale as well. Both readings are published; the earlier edition dropped the word 'core' outside the workbook, which made the concentration look higher than the whole bridge supports. It is high either way, as it is for any growing manufacturer discounted over five explicit years, and the terminal grid in the sensitivity section runs the whole range rather than quoting a comfortable part of it.

The terminal DEBT WEIGHT is derived, not asserted. Today's market-value net-debt weight is 25.1%; the forecast balance sheet, once funded, carries a book net-debt weight of 39.8% at FY2030E. The valuation uses the market-value reading, 25.1%, because a weighted average cost of capital weights market values; the book reading gives a terminal rate of 12.77% against 13.56% and is published beside it. The earlier edition used 20%, which is neither reading, and said it was reconciled to a balance sheet that did not balance.

[Book value and sustainable return] book value per share 37.00. Return on average equity was 24.6% in FY2024 and 26.5% in FY2025. The forecast path is 15.5% / 17.4% / 20.3% / 22.2% / 23.0% — it RISES THROUGH the window rather than settling, so the sustainable return used here is the MEAN OF ITS LAST THREE YEARS, 21.81%, computed from that path and not asserted. (The earlier edition described the same number as the level the forecast 'settles at', which the path does not do.) A sustainable-return multiple of (return 21.8% less growth 5%) over (perpetual cost of equity 14.90% less growth) is 1.698 times book, or 62.81 a share. Every term in that multiple is live: change beta, the terminal risk-free rate, the terminal premium or growth and the lens moves.

[Relative multiples] the company's OWN traded history is computable entirely from primary material — year-end closes against audited attributable profit: 4.7 times (2022), 6.6 times (2023), 6.2 times (2024), 8.7 times (2025), a four-year mean of 6.6. Each year divides that year's audited attributable profit by that year's WEIGHTED-AVERAGE share count, so the FY2025 reading uses 162.016 million shares rather than the 168.756 million now in issue — the capital increase completed during that year. At 130.05 the shares trade on 15.2 times trailing attributable earnings measured on the count in issue today, or 14.6 times on the audited weighted average; both readings are legitimate and both are published. The shares also trade on 11.8 times trailing EBITDA. The re-rating is the single most important fact about this share price: the earnings multiple has more than doubled against its own four-year history.

The lens triangulates three multiples rather than asserting one, and EACH IS APPLIED TO THE EARNINGS OF ITS OWN PERIOD. (1) The forward multiple this model's own economics justify: retention must equal growth 5% over sustainable return 21.8%, so the payout the multiple can assume is 77%, and 77% over (perpetual cost of equity 14.90% less growth) is 7.78 times — applied to 6.17 of FY2026E earnings a share. (2) The company's own four-year mean, 6.57 times, a TRAILING multiple applied to 8.54 of trailing earnings. (3) A struck reference of 21.35 times — the midpoint of the only two comparable observations available, 26.7 times for a listed Saudi Arabian generics manufacturer and about 16 times for larger international generic manufacturers, and NOT a median of a disclosed peer set — but those companies are Gulf-listed and face a cost of equity near 10%, not 14.9%; adjusted for that single difference the same reference implies 10.78 times, also on trailing earnings. The three give 48.04 / 56.15 / 92.09, averaging 65.42. Left unadjusted, the struck reference alone would give 182.39 — the size of that gap IS the country-risk discount, and it is shown rather than hidden inside a chosen multiple. The peers are not named and their financials are not published, so this third leg cannot be rebuilt from peer filings; that is a stated limitation of the leg, not a hidden one.

[Normalised earnings power] the three-year average operating margin is 22.9%, against 25.1% in FY2025 — so this lens deliberately gives back part of the best year. Applied to FY2027E revenue of 12,063 million, financed at the FY2027E cost of debt and taxed at 23.5%, with the normalised associate contribution added, that is EGP 8.40 a share of sustainable earnings. Capitalised at the PERPETUAL cost of equity of 14.90% less 5% growth, on the 77% payout that growth rate permits: 65.40 a share. Using today's crisis-level cost of equity of 25.57% in a perpetuity would be a category error — a steady-state multiple takes a steady-state rate.

[Synthesis] TWO centres, not one. The three lenses that do not turn on the contested judgement are Book value and sustainable return 62.81 · Relative multiples 65.42 · Normalised earnings power 65.40. Carrying them beside Frame A gives a weighted centre of 61.21; beside Frame B, 68.70. The two frames are NOT averaged into a single number — that is the study's standing rule and the earlier edition's single centre of 66.57 broke it, because weighting both frames at a quarter each is a straight average of them. The field across all five readings runs 58.04 to 73.03 against a 130.05 market price.

[The crux] the base build charges the new biologicals facility's depreciation and its interest — both mechanical consequences of the company's own disclosed December-2025 licensing — but carries NO revenue line for it, because the company has published no volume, price or utilisation guidance for the plant. So the crux is not what the plant is worth; it is how much it must sell. Solving the same model for the market price: an additional EGP 6,931 million of revenue by FY2030E at a 45% contribution margin closes the gap from 58.04 to 130.05. That is 28% of FY2030E revenue, or about USD 120 million a year — 1.20 times the USD 100 million the company says it invested in the plant. That number is observable: it is testable against the first year the company discloses biosimilar revenue.

Two things that must be published for that hurdle to be auditable, and were not before. THE RAMP: the incremental revenue is not dropped into the final year, it is phased 0% / 10% / 30% / 60% / 100% across FY2026E-FY2030E, and the same total placed entirely in FY2030E would be a lower and easier hurdle. THE REINVESTMENT: the incremental revenue is charged capital expenditure at the same share of revenue as the existing business and working capital on the same day ratios, so it faces the identical reinvestment discipline. The earlier edition let it arrive free of both and published a hurdle of about USD 115 million; charged properly it is USD 120 million.
